boundaries: Hardy-Weinberg assumptions (random mating, no selection/migration/mutation/drift, diploid sexual population) are part of the record, never footnotes.
Separate counts from frequencies, density from abundance, and discrete-time from continuous-time growth; continuous exponentials need exp and must be deferred with sources.
Concentration/dilution chemistry belongs to the chemistry lane: reference it, do not duplicate it.
Exclude epidemiology needing differential equations, phylogenetics, and any clinical, diagnostic or species-management interpretation.
No medical advice or health recommendations of any kind.
coverage_guidance: Priorities are seeds, not a finite checklist. Continue into adjacent source chapters/subtopics inside the boundaries, selecting independently reusable relationships. Save multiple bounded batches without waiting for owner review. Check supplied inventory and prior returns for equivalent relationships and conflicting IDs. Record out-of-format discoveries as deferred with exact sources and missing capabilities; do not force chains or dilute quality for a quota.
integration_expectation: Counts, frequencies and dimensionless factors; meanings (allele_frequency, genotype_frequency, growth_factor, population_density and similar) are new and require extension. Hardy-Weinberg, geometric growth, allometry and count ratios are scalar (+ - * / **) and fit the engine once meanings exist. Continuous exponentials and logarithms are out of profile: defer them, never approximate them.
mission: Curate atomic, reusable quantitative biology relationships: allele/genotype frequencies, discrete population growth, allometric scaling and density accounting, each with explicit biological assumptions. Continue through successive review batches during the sustained session; no ecological chain or field use case is required. This is quantitative formalization, not biological advice.
priorities: Hardy-Weinberg genotype frequencies from allele frequencies
Discrete (geometric) population growth over counted generations or periods
Allometric power scaling of a trait with body mass
Allele frequency from observed genotype counts
Population density from count and area
special_checks: Guard frequencies to [0,1] with sum-to-one references recomputed independently, not by repeating the identity
Never confuse the discrete growth factor R (dimensionless per-period multiplier) with a continuous rate r
Area units must be explicit for density; reject zero-area denominators
Allometric records must state fitted vs theoretical exponents and never present a fitted exponent as a law
starter_sources: https://openstax.org -- navigate to a Biology title and its chapters on Population Genetics and Population Ecology; record exact book, edition and section, never cite the root as evidence
https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov -- use Bookshelf references as discovery only; primary textbook evidence is preferred and the root alone proves nothing
title: Biology: population genetics, growth and ecological accounting
